title: Vulnerable dependency set requires targeted upgrades
evidence: npm audit reports 26 affected package entries: 1 critical, 18 high, 6 moderate, 1 low. Next 16.2.6 has critical advisories, but its server/image/OG paths are not the site runtime: Vinext aliases next APIs. react-server-dom-webpack 19.2.6 is present in the compiled Worker and has GHSA-wx67-qw84-cm4g. No application Server Actions exist. The image-size dependency is pinned to 2.0.2 through Vinext; image input is local public assets only. Dev-tool advisories must not be reported as confirmed production exploits.
action: Patch Next within the supported 16.x line and align React/React DOM/RSC to compatible patched versions; evaluate Vinext and tooling upgrades separately. Do not run npm audit fix --force (it proposes a Drizzle downgrade and Vinext major upgrade).
acceptance: Fresh lockfile install, build, all route/security tests, and re-audit; record residual advisories and their reachable entry points.
product_decision: Engineering dependency compatibility decision; no product decision.
effort: High uncertainty on external exploitability; medium upgrade effort

title: Inherited route-map properties crash rendering
evidence: Requests to /en/constructor, /en/__proto__, and /en/portal/constructor throw TypeErrors. The Node production server returns 500 for /en/constructor. Plain-object dictionary lookups accept inherited properties as page specifications. This is a request-scoped failure, not demonstrated prototype mutation or a site-wide outage.
action: Use own-property checks or null-prototype/Map registries consistently for route, alias, page-title, industry and portal lookups; reject unknown keys before rendering.
acceptance: Adversarial keys constructor, __proto__, toString and hasOwnProperty in both languages render a controlled missing-page response; valid routes stay unchanged.

title: Partnership form discards its prepared enquiry
evidence: submit only calls preventDefault and setSent(true). Inputs have no stored values or names; success unmounts the form. The ready state has no summary, no prepared mailto body and no edit action; preparing another enquiry resets the inputs. Live interaction timed out before returning a session ID, so no live submission or result is claimed.
action: Keep the draft and provide a reviewable summary and explicit email handoff, or clearly label this as an illustrative form. Use the established EnquiryForm pattern if email drafting is the intended contract.
acceptance: Synthetic draft survives review and edit, and the chosen handoff contains its fields; no unapproved backend write or automatic email.
product_decision: Confirm whether this route is an email draft or a real submission.
effort: Low root-cause uncertainty; product choice required

title: Membership wizard has no usable final handoff
evidence: The final step removes the review and shows onboarding links plus a portal preview, without a prepared email, copy/download action or submission. Primary industry and interest inputs are uncontrolled and unmount between steps. The plan query parameter emitted by membership cards is never read. The page correctly states nothing is submitted or paid, so this is a broken draft journey, not a failed payment or actual record loss.
action: Define the intended draft handoff, preserve all selected fields, honour the plan preselection, and keep review/back recovery through completion.
acceptance: Walk each membership plan, back/forward, review and finish with synthetic data; all chosen fields remain available in the approved handoff.
product_decision: Confirm the existing email-led enquiry contract and required draft fields; do not add payments, accounts or a database in this cleanup.
effort: Low code uncertainty; product choice required

title: Repository verification is already failing
evidence: npm test builds successfully but fails its content-routes suite. Direct execution identifies the stale Programmes & GBA label assertion (the header now uses shorter navLabel values); the normal worker test reporter only reports file-level failure. tsc --noEmit --incremental false fails with missing cloudflare:workers, Fetcher and D1Database types. No typecheck npm script or checked-in CI workflow is present.
action: Assert current semantic navigation contracts, generate Cloudflare binding/runtime types, and add a supported typecheck command plus suitable CI. Avoid changing product navigation to satisfy an obsolete test.
acceptance: Clean install, build, npm test, lint and typecheck pass on the supported Node version; test failure output identifies the failing assertion.
product_decision: None; current source is evidence of the navigation contract.
effort: Low uncertainty; Cloudflare type generation requires care

title: Unknown URLs return success or unrelated content
evidence: /en/not-a-page returns a missing-page UI with HTTP 200. /fr/events renders English; /robots.txt renders the homepage as HTML. Extra segments after a real event or join route are ignored. /api/notes is HTML, not the example API. The existing test explicitly expects 200 for a missing route.
action: Validate languages, route keys and segment counts at the server route boundary, use a real 404 response, and add an intentional robots route. Preserve documented aliases or redirect them explicitly.
acceptance: Assert status and content type for unknown locale, arbitrary path, extra segments and robots.txt; valid paths/aliases and bilingual canonical URLs stay correct.
product_decision: Confirm only if legacy aliases beyond the current documented routes must be preserved.

title: Form validation and acknowledgement controls are inconsistent
evidence: EnquiryForm disables native validation with noValidate but checks only nonempty fields, including email. Join and newsletter accept anything containing @. The join review required checkbox is outside a form and is not read by next(), so it cannot gate completion. There is no backend transmission here; this does not prove unauthorized processing of personal data.
action: Validate email using a consistent approach; trim required fields; make acknowledgement state explicit and enforce it before the existing final draft action. Add reasonable draft-length limits and clear error focus.
acceptance: Invalid and whitespace-only values are rejected; unchecked acknowledgement cannot complete; valid drafts remain editable and mailto text is correctly encoded.
product_decision: Confirm acknowledgement wording and the final draft contract before changing consent semantics.

title: Search and directory controls imply unsupported behaviour
evidence: Site search echoes the entered query and shows the same five route cards; it never searches content. Directory filter and sort buttons have no handlers. Solution categories change visual selection only, while no solution records exist. These are public discovery placeholders, not an authorization or database defect.
action: Choose clear browse/preview copy or implement a bounded approved search dataset; disable unsupported controls or explain their state.
acceptance: A user can tell which controls perform a search, and every enabled control has observable, relevant results or a clear empty state.
product_decision: Decide preview versus functional discovery before implementation.

title: Dormant D1 example is unsafe to activate unchanged
evidence: The example exposes raw exception messages, has no ownership/auth checks, assumes payload field types before trim, and returns 500 for malformed JSON. The real schema is empty, bindings are null, and db:generate reports 0 tables because it targets db/schema.ts rather than the example schema. It is outside app/, so it is not an active notes API vulnerability.
action: Keep example explicitly opt-in; before activation add authenticated ownership, runtime input validation, safe generic errors and a matching schema/migration path. Do not copy this file into app/api unchanged.
acceptance: An isolated example test rejects malformed input, cannot read another user’s notes, returns safe errors, and applies its migration to a disposable D1 database.
product_decision: Choose whether optional persistence is wanted at all.
effort: Low source uncertainty; not a current production exploit

title: Shadowed page implementations increase maintenance risk
evidence_status: verified by route precedence and source
evidence: ExpansionRoute runs first. EventsPage and GbaPage fallback implementations are unreachable for their supported paths. StandardPage branches for why-wisetech, ai-plus, insights, partner-with-us, about, ai-transparency and ai-ops are shadowed by ExpansionRoute. ProgrammesPage’s detail branch is also unreachable: the caller only uses it for the top-level catalogue. These are not removable based on reference counts alone.
action: Remove only branches proven shadowed, retaining the shared catalogue/homepage components and pending record states that are reachable.
acceptance: Rendered output and navigation for every supported EN/ZH route remain equivalent, with route reachability checks.

title: Optional starter dependencies remain in the application install
paths: package.json:18; package.json:31; db/index.ts:1; db/schema.ts:1; drizzle.config.ts:1; README.md:25
evidence: drizzle-orm and drizzle-kit support only the unused D1 adapter/example and migration scaffolding. No application route imports getDb; D1/R2 bindings are disabled. This is dormant optional tooling rather than conclusive unused-package proof. Vite, Vinext, React plugins and RSC are framework/runtime or peer dependencies; Next supplies types/tooling despite runtime aliases, so generic import scanning is insufficient for removal.
action: If the starter scaffolding is no longer wanted, remove its files, scripts, docs and dependencies together; otherwise isolate the example install and document opt-in steps.
acceptance: Clean install/build and all route checks work without the removed scaffold; lockfile and README match package.json.
product_decision: Confirm whether optional D1 support should remain available.

title: Ten public assets have no in-repository consumers
paths: public/hero-wise-hk.png; public/og.png; public/editorial/; public/favicon.svg; public/file.svg; public/globe.svg; public/window.svg
evidence_status: verified by tracked-file reference scan; external use unknown
evidence: Ten candidates total 3,106,935 bytes: four unused editorial WebP files, hero-wise-hk.png, og.png and four SVGs. Current visuals use archive photos; metadata points to og-wtia-blue.png and the WTIA favicon. Public URLs may still be externally referenced, so no assets were deleted.
action: Confirm external references and remove or archive unused files; preserve any intentional public URL contract.
acceptance: No source/metadata references or rendered-image checks break; redirects/retention are applied where external URLs must survive.
product_decision: Only external public-URL retention needs an owner decision.

title: No application-level error recovery for render failures
evidence_status: verified locally; availability of platform logging not established
evidence: There is no app/error.tsx or global-error.tsx. The demonstrated route crash returns a generic Internal Server Error in the Node production server, without a localized retry/recovery screen. Core public routes pass; no broad outage is demonstrated.
action: Fix known input-triggered crashes first, then add a localized error boundary with retry/home/contact actions and sanitized server diagnostics.
acceptance: Injected render failure yields a controlled response and useful recovery without leaking stack traces or personal data; normal navigation still works.

title: Metadata and URL ownership have drift points
evidence: Site origin is hardcoded in three places. Programme aliases hkict/asa/tct render canonical content but only AI-industry aliases are normalized in metadata. All pages inherit og:url for the base origin. Production samples also retain codex-preview=development; the existing test requires it. This needs an explicit environment contract, not an unreviewed removal.
action: Centralize the approved site origin and canonical alias registry, derive route-specific social URLs, and distinguish preview metadata from production if the hosting contract permits it.
acceptance: Canonical, hreflang, OG URL and sitemap agree for both languages and all aliases on each environment.
product_decision: Confirm the authoritative public origin and required Sites preview marker contract.

title: Event filters and navigation do not preserve valid query state reliably
evidence: Filter values are accepted from arbitrary URL strings without checking available options. Unknown status values bypass the open/completed conditions; unrelated query parameters are discarded by replaceState. The language switch builds only the pathname, dropping a visitor’s event filter query. These are small public-state correctness issues, not private-data leaks.
action: Parse allowlisted filter values, choose a documented policy for unrelated query parameters, and preserve supported state across language switches.
acceptance: Invalid query values normalize predictably; back/forward and EN/ZH switches retain supported filters without changing record status.
product_decision: None for validation; agree whether unrelated campaign parameters should be retained.

title: Concierge suggestions promise queries its static response cannot answer
evidence: Event prompts include retail relevance and Cantonese events, but reply() ignores which prompt was chosen and returns the same ecosystem sentence outside membership/join. The arrow text is not an actionable source link. No LLM call, external transmission, or private member data access occurs in this implementation.
action: Keep the static guide within its supported scope, with prompt-specific approved answers and actual links; do not introduce an AI service as cleanup.
acceptance: Every visible prompt returns a relevant approved answer and working next step in both languages, with an honest boundary on unsupported requests.
product_decision: Confirm whether this remains a static guide and who approves answers.
